source.title: Models of Heavy-Tailed Mechanistic Universality
source.authors: Liam Hodgkinson; Zhi-Chao Wang; Michael W. Mahoney

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents reading relevant material.
record.tranche_reason: The paper derives a theoretical relationship between feature-matrix spectra and generalization error, and reports spectral measurements on trained networks. Its experiments do not test the claim versions’ training-versus-test generalization gaps; its theoretical scaling result addresses generalization under a restricted synthetic ridge-regression setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports near-zero training loss and 100% training accuracy for CIFAR-10 networks, and plots/characterizes spectral distributions. Those spectral outcomes do not measure the training-to-test gap or the properties named in V1–V8. Its theoretical generalization-error proposition is on the subject of the claim, but does not test any listed version, which concerns empirical coexistence, width, architecture, optimizer comparisons, batch-size penalties, dropout, sharpness rankings, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study develops heavy-tailed spectral models and a restricted ridge-regression scaling law, but its own results test none of V1–V8. Figures 1–2 report spectra and training fit, without held-out performance comparisons. Spectral tails do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking of generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors propose a spectral framework in which data covariance and feature-matrix structure contribute to heavy tails, and apply it to restricted scaling laws, optimizer trajectories and spectral training phases. They explicitly defer precise connections between generalization and their model hyperparameters.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical random-matrix and entropic-regularization model, with spectral experiments; it does not reproduce the interventions or generalization-gap measurements in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The plotted weight-matrix spectral behavior varies with batch size; the authors report heavier-tailed spectra at smaller batch sizes and rank deficiency at batch size 5. This is a spectral outcome, not a test-error comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Proposition 5.1 derives an asymptotic prediction-error scaling law for noiseless, isotropic ridge regression with an assumed feature-spectrum distribution and a shrinking ridge parameter.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated ridge-regression assumptions, prediction-error scaling depends jointly on feature-spectrum parameters and ridge-parameter scaling.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2 and Appendix A.2 show MiniAlexNet weight spectra changing from random-like at batch size 1000 to heavier-tailed at smaller batches, with significant rank deficiency at batch size 5. No held-out performance is reported; training stops at loss below 0.01 or 200 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size changes trained MiniAlexNet weight spectra under the tested learning-rate and stopping recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 and Appendix A.1 report inverse-Gamma behavior near zero in NTK spectra for VGG11, ResNet9 and ResNet18 before and after training on 1000 CIFAR-10 examples. The reported 100% accuracy is training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NTK spectra in the tested convolutional networks exhibit inverse-Gamma behavior near zero.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The relevant spectral experiment trains only on 1000 CIFAR-10 examples and reports no held-out metrics. The generalization result is a theoretical proposition for isotropic ridge regression under restrictive assumptions, not an empirical test of the listed versions. Spectral evidence includes plots, and the authors explicitly defer precise links between generalization and their hyperparameters.
record.rows_left_out: No results meet the row criteria for the listed versions. The spectral fits and batch-size-dependent spectral changes do not measure the generalization gap or the version-specific outcomes.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and fixed-random-label training, including held-out accuracy in both conditions.
Test error as network width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contributions of locality or convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under specified tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across dropout configurations, training-set sizes and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with measured generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. Empty version-linked rows and verdicts are appropriate. Appendix A.1 explicitly uses 1000 training examples; Appendix A.2 does not explicitly establish that the MiniAlexNet batch-size experiment uses that same subsample.

versions.untested_parts: Whether the same models and recipes fit fixed random labels and generalize on natural labels; held-out natural-label accuracy and random-label chance performance.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and resulting test error on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
Convolutional versus fully connected test-error comparisons and the effects of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive-optimizer versus SGD held-out comparisons and tuning or weight-decay conditions.
Large- versus small-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout intervention effects on held-out error across data-size regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurement and its ranking of generalization gaps against other measures.
Removal of memorized examples and its effect on test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
